citation: Stewart K, Subramanian D, Neal U, Hanson AJ. APOE Genotype Influences Postprandial Blood Pressure After High fat Feeding in Older Adults. J Nutr Health Aging. 2019;23(5):408-413.
protocol: After a 12 h fast, one breakfast-style meal of about 700 kcal in random order: high-fat meal (30% carbohydrate, 50% fat, 20% protein of energy; GI >70) or high-carbohydrate meal (55% carbohydrate, 25% fat, 20% protein; GI <55); BP, HR and glucose at 7 time points to about 240 min (15, 60 and 180 min named in text).
population: 32 cognitively healthy older adults (22 female; 14 APOE E4-, 18 E4+), age 55-84 (E4- 66.1 +/- 6.4 y, E4+ 63.7 +/- 6.9 y); 8 with hypertension (3 on medication); BMI in Table 1 (row not cleanly extractable from the XML); no diabetes.
note: Healthy older adults, crossover. Watch: the printed SBP value is a net AUC of change from baseline over 4 h, not a mean at stated minutes; the time-course means for SBP, DBP and HR are figure-only (Figures 2-3), and DBP has no printed numbers in table or text. Macronutrients are given as % of energy, not grams. HR text value has no uncertainty.
